posts.title: Direct-method cash flow statements
posts.source_date_evidence: Public LinkedIn SocialMediaPosting.datePublished metadata retrieved 27 October 2026
posts.original_post_text:
Once upon a time it was common to see citations of Accounting Trends and Techniques for a statistic along the lines of "despite the direct method being encouraged by standards, only 1% of firms use it to report cash flows from operating activities."

However, Accounting Trends and Techniques stopped providing statistics in 2011.

So what's the situation today?

To address this question, I used data from XBRL filings compiled using my `dera.pq` package. The answer: about 0.2% of 10-K filings today provide direct-method statements of cash flows. The note below has more detailed information.

The note below also provides some discussion of how to work with XBRL data and the challenges in doing so.

#xbrl
posts.dated_update: The 0.2% figure is the finding reported with the original post on 11 June 2026. The [maintained HTML analysis](https://iangow.github.io/notes/cash-flows/index.html) was updated on 23 October 2026; its [PDF edition](https://iangow.github.io/notes/cash-flows/cash-flows.pdf) is dated 11 June 2026. The methods and qualifications are in that analysis.

Added a dated context note anchoring the 0.2% finding to the original 11 June 2026 post and linking the existing HTML/PDF editions.

posts.title: Moving notes to Typst
posts.source_date_evidence: Public LinkedIn SocialMediaPosting.datePublished metadata retrieved 27 October 2026
posts.original_post_text:
I barely know what Typst is. What I do know is that it comes bundled with Quarto (hence Positron/RStudio), requires very little change to my markdown code, yet compiles much, much faster than LaTeX. 

With a few tweaks here and there, I migrated the construction site that contains most of the various "notes" I've posted to LinkedIn from LaTeX to Typst today. Some Band-Aid code was eliminated and I think the PDFs even look better: https://lnkd.in/egWq76je

More "notes" are here (most with links to PDFs): https://lnkd.in/embi_a_t
posts.dated_update: The links above now lead to the maintained notes collection and chronological archive. The [Quarto sources](https://github.com/iangow/notes) record the output format for each note in its `.qmd` file.
